sources.title: R. Eymard, T. Gallouët, and R. Herbin, Finite Volume Methods, updated author text
sources.locator: Complete updated 254-page author text inspected; Chapter 9 §§9.2–9.3, PDF pp. 38–47, covering orthogonal TPFA fluxes, transmissibilities, conservative balances, and maximum-principle conditions.

contents.name: Chapter 9 §9.2: orthogonal TPFA mesh and face transmissibility
contents.reason: The local specialization uses shared positive interior conductances from the actual PE13 TPFA interface, removes boundary fluxes for homogeneous no-flux data, and states no accuracy claim for arbitrary admissible meshes.

contents.name: Chapter 9 §9.3: conservative TPFA cell balances and diffusion energy structure
contents.reason: The local proof verifies interval preservation and weighted mass directly for the no-flux stiffness matrix and periodic centered matrix; it does not import a Dirichlet maximum principle as a no-flux result.

contents.name: Chapter 9 §§9.2–9.3: cell-centered Cartesian no-flux specialization
contents.reason: This item fixes a uniform orthogonal cell-centered grid and its reflected ghost-value convention as a concrete no-flux TPFA branch.

contents.name: Chapter 9 §§9.2–9.3: finite-volume boundary conventions
contents.reason: The error proof uses the actual no-flux Cartesian operator and even reflection; its smooth compatibility hypothesis is stated rather than inferred from generic Neumann data.

sources.title: Jérôme Droniou, Finite volume schemes for diffusion equations: introduction to and review of modern methods, 2014
sources.locator: Complete 38-page review inspected; §1.3 and §§2–2.2, PDF pp. 6–10, covering monotonicity, TPFA orthogonality, and transmissibility conditions.

contents.name: §1.3: monotone finite-volume diffusion and M-matrix sign structure
contents.reason: The local finite-matrix proof supplies nonnegative semigroup weights and conservation for the specified TPFA and periodic operators, including the no-flux case.

contents.name: §2: TPFA diffusion on orthogonal meshes
contents.reason: The local item explicitly inherits the orthogonality and positive transmissibility hypotheses and limits the claim to the scalar TPFA operator.

contents.name: §2.2: TPFA consistency restrictions
contents.reason: The rectangular grid satisfies the needed orthogonality directly; the page warns that the positivity proof does not establish accuracy on general nonorthogonal or arbitrary polyhedral meshes.

sources.title: Willem Hundsdorfer, Numerical Solution of Advection-Diffusion-Reaction Equations, lecture notes for Ph.D. course, 1996
sources.locator: Complete 93-page notes inspected; §4 printed pp. 25–29, §6 printed pp. 37–41, and §9 printed pp. 60–64, covering positive diffusion discretizations, reaction signs, Euler restrictions, and Lie splitting.

contents.name: §4: positivity of semidiscrete reaction and diffusion equations
contents.reason: The local proof extends the face-sign argument to compact rectangles, proves global continuation, and separately derives the stoichiometric mass conclusion.

contents.name: §6: forward-Euler reaction positivity and its step restriction
contents.reason: The local coordinatewise proof gives the rectangle and mass version with an explicit bound, and the Fisher–KPP example checks the scalar endpoint calculation.

contents.name: §9: reaction-then-diffusion Lie composition and local commutator defect
contents.reason: The algorithm fixes this ordering, while the finite-grid commutator and error theorem are proved locally with constants independent of the periodic mesh.

contents.name: §9: mesh-uniform splitting-error requirements
contents.reason: The error proof establishes its own periodic semigroup contraction, residual estimate, commutator control, and recurrence instead of importing a finite-dimensional estimate with mesh-dependent constants.

sources.title: Luca Doria, Numerical Algorithms, lecture notes, Johannes Gutenberg-Universität Mainz, 2022
sources.locator: Complete 190-page notes inspected; §§10.6–10.8, PDF pp. 149–153, covering vector reaction-diffusion systems, homogeneous-mode linearization, dispersion matrices, and a FitzHugh–Nagumo illustration.

contents.name: §10.6: vector reaction-diffusion equations and homogeneous equilibria
contents.reason: The local definition fixes the continuous diagonal-diffusion model and separately states its periodic and homogeneous no-flux domains.

contents.name: §10.7: two-species diffusion-dependent dispersion matrix
contents.reason: The proposition derives the trace-determinant test for each actual continuous or discrete Laplacian eigenvalue and states the strict unstable-band condition.

contents.name: §10.7: general linear mode analysis; explicit example computed locally
contents.reason: The example recomputes the equilibrium, Jacobian, dispersion polynomial, and one unstable continuous torus mode explicitly. Source attribution corrected at Step 3a: the Brusselator and its finite-grid comparison are local calculations, not the model in source §10.8.

contents.name: §10.7: general linear mode analysis; explicit example computed locally
contents.reason: The example substitutes the exact three-node periodic eigenvalues and proves that all grid modes are stable despite the continuous unstable mode. Source attribution corrected at Step 3a: the Brusselator and its finite-grid comparison are local calculations, not the model in source §10.8.
